sources.notes: Authorized Google Books listing for the 2009 Harper Collins paperback, ISBN 9780061755668. Confirms the same work family and highlights key concepts: survival instincts, the face as an unreliable sole signal, feet/thumbs/eyelids, confidence displays, and trust/authority cues.

sources.title: The Psychology of Body Language
sources.notes: Joe Navarro article reinforcing the book's observational frame: nonverbal communication is expressed across the body, comfort/discomfort patterns matter, and feet/torso orientation can reveal preference before words do.

sources.title: The Truth About Lie Detection
sources.notes: Joe Navarro article explicitly warning that humans are no better than chance at lie detection and that behavior is better treated as evidence of discomfort, stress, or unresolved issues than as proof of lying.

sources.title: Nonverbals of the Skin
sources.notes: Joe Navarro article expanding on physiological comfort/discomfort displays, ventilating behaviors, blushing/paling, goosebumps, self-soothing touch, and the caution that stress signals are not equivalent to deception.

sources.title: Reserved Behaviors of the Hands
sources.role: chapter-specific support for hands and fingers
sources.notes: Joe Navarro article emphasizing that hands remain highly expressive at a distance and that finger interlacing, rubbing, and palm-up tension behaviors are useful stress indicators.
